test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 17th November 2021 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What is the difference between the compound interest on ₹3,000 for 1 year at 5% per annum compounded yearly and that compounded half - yearly ?
solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs.3000 and Rate % = 5% per annum

**Formula used:**

Amount = Principal × (1 + R/100)ⁿ

Compound Interest (CI) = [P × (1 + R/100)ⁿ - P]

Where P = principal, R = rate %, n = time

Effective Rate of interest when compounded half yearly at R % for one year

⇒ Rₑffₑ꜀ₜᵢvₑ = R% + R% + R%²/100

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

When compounded yearly, rate = 5%, n = 1

CI = 3000 × (1 + 5/100) - 3000

⇒ CI (yearly) = 3000 × 5/100 = 150

When compounded half-yearly,

Rate = 5/2% = 2.5%, n = 2

CI = 3000 × [(1 + 2.5/100)² - 1]

⇒ 3000 × (1.025² - 1) = 3000 × .050625

⇒ CI (half yearly) = 151.875

CI (half yearly) - CI (yearly) = 151.875 - 150

⇒ 1.875 = Rs. 1(7)/(8) 

∴ **The difference between the compound interest compounded half yearly and yearly is Rs. 1(7)/(8)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**Rate of interest when compounded yearly = 5%

When compounded half-yearly, 

Rate (half yearly) = 5/2 = 2.5%

As this will be compounded every 6 months for 1 year, 

Hence the effective rate of interest will be = 2.5% + 2.5% + 2.5%²/100

⇒ Rₑffₑ꜀ₜᵢvₑ= 5.0625%

∴ Difference in CI = 3000 × (Rₑffₑ꜀ₜᵢvₑ - R)

⇒ 3000 × (5.0625% - 5%) = 3000 × 0.0625/100

⇒ 1.875 = Rs. 1(7)/(8)

**∴ The difference between the compound interest compounded half yearly and yearly is Rs. 1(7)/(8)**
